title: Generation of a squamous cell carcinoma mouse model for lineage tracing of BMI1+ cancer stem cells
protocol: Inject Bmi1CreER; R26tdTomato mice intraperitoneally with tamoxifen at a dose of 225 mg per 1 kg body weight 24 h before sacrificing the mice for labeling BMI1+ CSCs.
Inject mice bearing HNSCC intraperitoneally with EdU at a dose of 25 μg/g body weight after reaching the experimental endpoint to label proliferating tumor cells.
Euthanize mice using CO2 asphyxiation 90 min after EdU injection.
Pin mouse limbs to the dissection board using needles to secure the body.
Spray the body with 70% ethanol.
Use forceps to grab the skin and cut a long incision through the midline from the chin to the upper chest region of the mouse using scissors.
Gently insert scissors under the skin to separate the skin from the underlying tissues.
Cut and open the skin laterally at the chest level once fully detached, and pin the skin with needles to expose the cervical lymph nodes.
Carefully excise the lymph nodes with sharp scissors under the Leica EZ4 Stereo Microscope (Use hemostatic cotton to swab the blood that might hinder the identification of the lymph nodes).
Place the lymph nodes into a 15 mL falcon tube filled with 10 mL 4% PFA at 22°C–25°C.
Cut the joints on both sides of the jaws with a bone scissor.
Open the jaws as wide as possible to expose the tongue tissues.
Cut the whole tongue using a sharp scissor.
Take photos of the tongue using the Leica EZ4 Stereo Microscope with a ruler.
Put the tongue in the 4% PFA tube mentioned above (The tissue can be kept in 4% PFA up to 72 h before over-fixation).
After 24 hours, remove PFA and wash the tongue and lymph nodes three times with PBS for 30 minutes at 22°C–25°C.
Cut the tongue into halves sagittally along the mid-line of the HNSCC lesion.
Keep half of the lesion for paraffin section and the other half for cryosection.
Discard PBS and pour in 10 mL of 30% sucrose solution in PBS into the 15 mL tube.
Keep the tissue at 4°C for 48 h until the tissue sinks in the solution.
Embed the tissue in pre-chilled optimal cutting temperature (OCT) compound in an appropriate embedding mold.
Freeze on dry ice and store tissue at -80°C until sectioning.
Cut the cytosections at a thickness of 8–10 μm using a Leica cryostat and collect the sections with Superfrost Slides.
Let the slides dry for 5 min at 22°C–25°C.
Fix in 4% PFA for 10 min in a humidified chamber, 200 μL/sample, and spread with a new pipette tip.
Wash the slides in PBS for 5 min three times.
Make blocking buffer (5% Normal Donkey Serum, 1% bovine serum albumin, 0.2% Triton X-100 in 1 × PBS).
Trace around the sections with a pap pen and add 200–400 μL block buffer per slide.
Block in a humidified chamber for 30 min at 22°C–25°C.
Decant block buffer and add anti-pan-cytokeratin antibodies diluted in block buffer to each slide (200 μL per slide) and cover with a plastic coverslip.
Stain cervical lymph node sections with anti-pan-cytokeratin antibodies.
Incubate the stained sections at 4°C in a humidified chamber.
Remove coverslip by dipping in PBS until it slips off on its own.
Place slide into a Coplin jar containing 1 × PBS/0.1% Triton x-100 (PBS-T).
Wash for 5 minutes.
Repeat wash in PBS-T two more times, each for 5 minutes.
Dilute secondary antibodies in PBS-T at a ratio of 1:200 and add 200–300 μL per slide without coverslip.
Incubate the slides with diluted secondary antibodies at 22°C-25°C in a humidified chamber for 45 minutes.
Wash the slides three times in PBS-T, each wash lasting 5 minutes.
Wash the slides two more times in PBS (no Triton) for 5 minutes each.
Dip slide in deionized water and add 1–2 drops of Vectashield with DAPI.
Place glass coverslip over the slide carefully to avoid trapping bubbles.
Fix the slide around the coverslip with nail polish.
Acquire images using a fluorescent microscope running CellSens software.
Transfer tissue to 80% ethanol for 30 minutes at 22°C-25°C.
Transfer tissue to 95% ethanol for 30 minutes at 22°C-25°C.
Transfer tissue to 100% ethanol for 30 minutes at 22°C-25°C.
Repeat this step twice.
Transfer tissue to Histoclear II for 30 minutes at 22°C-25°C.
Repeat this step twice.
Incubate tissue in melted paraffin at 56°C-58°C for 30 minutes.
Transfer tissue into a labeled cassette.
Embed and label the tissue accordingly.
Cut the paraffin section to a thickness of 5 μm using a Leica RM2235 manual microtome.
Collect the sections with Superfrost Slides (Fisher Scientific Cat#12-550-15).
Deparaffinize the sections in Histoclear II for 3 minutes at 22°C-25°C.
Repeat this step twice.
Rehydrate the sections into 100% ethanol solution for 1 minute at 22°C-25°C.
Transfer the sections into 95% ethanol solution for 1 minute at 22°C-25°C.
Transfer the sections into 80% ethanol solution for 1 minute at 22°C-25°C.
Transfer the sections into 70% ethanol solution for 1 minute at 22°C-25°C.
Transfer the sections into deionized H2O for 5 minutes at 22°C-25°C.
Perform H&E staining using a H&E Staining Kit (Abcam, ab245880) according to the manufacturer’s guidance.
Mount the slides with Permount Mounting Medium.
Cover the mounted slides with a cover slide.
Air dry the slides in the chemical hood for 14–16 h.
Acquire images using microscopy running CellSens software.
